# ipapi.is

> IP address API and databases: who owns an IPv4 or IPv6 address (company, ASN, abuse contact), its reverse DNS hostname, where it is, and whether it belongs to a datacenter, VPN, proxy, Tor node or known abuser. A person creates the account once; after that everything below works with its API key and no browser, so scripts and AI agents can run it unattended.

## Accounts are created by a person

The dashboard at https://ipapi.is/app/ is protected by bot detection. Sign-up refuses automated and headless browsers, and no account can be created from a datacenter, VPN, proxy or Tor address. So a person signs up at https://ipapi.is/app/signup, in a normal browser on their normal connection, and copies the API key from https://ipapi.is/app/home. Don't script the dashboard: automated sign-ins may be refused, and can get a free account suspended.

From then on the key does the rest, as below: lookups, plan and usage, subscriptions, invoices, database downloads, data corrections, cancelling a subscription and replacing the key. Every change made with the key is mailed to the account. Keep the key on a server, since it can also read the invoices and cancel the subscriptions.

What stays with the person: paying (subscriptions at https://ipapi.is/app/sub and one-time credits at https://ipapi.is/app/otp, through Stripe or PayPal checkout) and accepting changed Terms of Service at the next sign-in.

A free account includes 1,000 lookups per day, commercial use included. Plans and prices: https://ipapi.is/pricing.html.

## Lookups

- `GET https://api.ipapi.is/?q=<IP or AS number>&key=<API key>` returns one JSON object. Leave out `q` to look up the caller's own address.
- `POST https://api.ipapi.is/` with the JSON body `{"ips": ["1.1.1.1", "AS15169"], "key": "<API key>"}` looks up to 100 entries at once. A key in the body stays out of URLs and logs.
- Without a key: 30 lookups per IP address per UTC day, with ownership, reverse DNS hostname and location only and no detection flags. Bulk lookups and AS number queries need a key.
- Errors are JSON with `error` and a stable `error_code`. A `429` carries `Retry-After`. A key's daily limit resets at 00:00 UTC.

## Your account, with the same key

Send the key as the query parameter `key`, or for a `POST` as `key` in the JSON body; without a valid one the answer is `401`.

- `GET https://ipapi.is/app/api/account?key=<API key>`: plan, daily limit, requests used today, credits, the databases you can download, and requests per day for the last 30 days.
- `GET https://ipapi.is/app/api/subscriptions?key=<API key>`: every subscription billed through Stripe or PayPal, with its `id`, price, `renewsAt` and, once cancelled, `endsAt`.
- `POST https://ipapi.is/app/api/subscriptions/cancel` with `{"key": "<API key>", "id": "<subscription id>"}`: cancels it at the end of the period already paid for. A plan billed through PayPal is cancelled in the PayPal account instead.
- `POST https://ipapi.is/app/api/key/rotate` with `{"key": "<API key>"}`: returns `{"key": "<new key>"}`. The old key stops working at once.
- `GET https://ipapi.is/app/api/invoices?key=<API key>`: every invoice with its number, date, amount and a PDF `url` (add `?key=<API key>` to fetch it).
- `GET https://ipapi.is/app/api/invoices.zip?key=<API key>`: all invoices as one ZIP archive.
- `GET https://ipapi.is/app/api/databases?key=<API key>`: every file the account can download right now, each with its `type`, `file` name, `released` date, size in `bytes` and download `url` (add `&key=<API key>` to fetch it). The file name changes with every release, so compare it with the last download before fetching a file again. A Business subscription also lists the full database dumps and the self-hosted API server with its `.ipdb` database.
- `POST https://ipapi.is/app/api-corrections` with `{"key": "<API key>", "type": "general" or "geofeed", "data": {...}}`: report wrong data. The formats are at https://ipapi.is/corrections-via-api.html.

## Documentation

- [API documentation](https://ipapi.is/developers.html): parameters, bulk lookups, every response field
- [Account API](https://ipapi.is/developers.html#account-api): plan, usage, subscriptions, invoices and database downloads for scripts and agents
- [OpenAPI](https://ipapi.is/openapi.json): every endpoint above with its parameters and response fields, for agent frameworks and client generators
- [Free tier](https://ipapi.is/free-tier.html): what a request without a key returns
- [Pricing](https://ipapi.is/pricing.html)
- [Status](https://ipapi.is/status.html): health and response time of every API server

<script>
  // content-visibility: auto defers rendering of below-the-fold sections, so
  // their heights are only estimates until they are rendered. Anchor jumps
  // (e.g. /#frequently-asked-questions from the footer) therefore land at the
  // wrong scroll position. After load, instantly correct the scroll position
  // until it is stable: each correction renders more deferred content, which
  // can shift the layout again.
  if (location.hash) {
    window.addEventListener('load', function () {
      var target = document.getElementById(decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1)));
      if (!target) return;
      var attempts = 0;
      (function settle() {
        var top = target.getBoundingClientRect().top;
        if (Math.abs(top) > 2 && attempts++ < 10) {
          window.scrollBy({ top: top, behavior: 'instant' });
          requestAnimationFrame(settle);
        }
      })();
    });
  }
</script>

<section id="frequently-asked-questions" class="section section-spacing faq-container deferred-section">
  <div class="container">
    <div class="section-intro">
      <h2 class="title is-2">Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
    </div>
    <div class="faq">
      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-header">
          <p class="card-header-title">What is ipapi.is?</p>
          <a class="card-header-icon">
            <span class="icon"><i class="fa-solid fa-angle-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
          </a>
        </div>
        <div class="card-content">
          <div class="content">
            <p>ipapi.is is a fast and accurate IP address API. It can be used to get meta information about any IPv4
              or IPv6 address on the Internet.</p>
            <p>Our clients use <a href="https://ipapi.is/">ipapi.is</a> for many different purposes:</p>
            <ul>
              <li>Blocking malicious traffic from accessing their services (such as data center, Tor, or proxy/VPN
                traffic).</li>
              <li>Traffic classification: Our clients want to know the composition of their traffic. Is it normal
                residential ISP traffic (<code>isp</code>) or does a majority of the requests originate from hosting
                providers (<code>hosting</code>)?</li>
              <li>Some customers need accurate IP geolocation intelligence. This is necessary for launching targeted
                advertising campaigns or enforcing specific location-based actions (only EU traffic allowed, only US
                traffic allowed, etc.).</li>
            </ul>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-header">
          <p class="card-header-title">
            Is the API stable? How many servers are behind ipapi.is?
          </p>
          <a class="card-header-icon">
            <span class="icon"><i class="fa-solid fa-angle-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
          </a>
        </div>
        <div class="card-content">
          <div class="content">
            <p>The API runs on a multi-region fleet of dedicated Go servers across four global regions:</p>
            <ul>
              <li>United States — East & Central (<a href="https://us.ipapi.is/" rel="noopener noreferrer">us.ipapi.is</a>)</li>
              <li>Europe — Germany (<a href="https://de.ipapi.is/" rel="noopener noreferrer">de.ipapi.is</a>)</li>
              <li>Singapore (<a href="https://sg.ipapi.is/" rel="noopener noreferrer">sg.ipapi.is</a>)</li>
              <li>Japan — Osaka</li>
            </ul>
            <p><a href="https://api.ipapi.is/">api.ipapi.is</a> uses <strong>Azure Cloud DNS</strong> and
              <strong>Azure Traffic Manager</strong> to automatically route every request to the lowest-latency
              healthy server across multiple cloud providers. Live fleet health is published on the
              <a href="/status.html">API Status</a> page.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-header">
          <p class="card-header-title">Why was ipapi.is developed?</p>
          <a class="card-header-icon">
            <span class="icon"><i class="fa-solid fa-angle-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
          </a>
        </div>
        <div class="card-content">
          <div class="content">
            <p>Initially, <a href="/">ipapi.is</a> was developed to provide accurate and reliable IP address data as a
              foundation for more complex IT security products. During development, we realized that many other
              organizations also need such basic (but accurate) IP data.</p>
            <p><a href="/">ipapi.is</a> is technically a simple service that does not deal with live end-user traffic
              and its complex consequences.</p>
            <p>However, our biggest challenge with <a href="/">ipapi.is</a> is to provide basic IP address data in the
              most reliable, accurate, and updated manner possible. By providing this reliable data, your more complex
              IT security solutions and decisions will stand on a robust foundation.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-header">
          <p class="card-header-title">What are the use cases of the API?</p>
          <a class="card-header-icon">
            <span class="icon"><i class="fa-solid fa-angle-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
          </a>
        </div>
        <div class="card-content">
          <div class="content">
            <p>IP address data can be used in many different ways:</p>
            <ul>
              <li>Geolocation: Determining the geographic location of a device connected to the Internet.</li>
              <li>IP reputation: Identifying whether an IP address has been associated with spam or malicious
                activity.</li>
              <li>Network troubleshooting: Identifying connectivity issues and diagnosing network problems.</li>
              <li>IT security: Tracking the source of cyberattacks and implementing security measures to prevent them.
              </li>
              <li>Targeted advertising: Using IP address data to target advertisements to specific regions or traffic
                types (e.g., locating only US visitors and excluding <code>hosting</code> traffic).</li>
              <li>Personalization: Customizing website content based on the visitor's geographic location.</li>
              <li>Analytics: Analyzing website traffic and visitor behavior based on their IP address.</li>
            </ul>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-header">
          <p class="card-header-title">How often is the API updated?</p>
          <a class="card-header-icon">
            <span class="icon"><i class="fa-solid fa-angle-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
          </a>
        </div>
        <div class="card-content">
          <div class="content">
            <p>The core API data is updated every week. Fast-moving data, such as VPN exit nodes and abuser
              intelligence, is updated daily.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-header">
          <p class="card-header-title">Can I self-host the ipapi.is API in my own infrastructure?</p>
          <a class="card-header-icon">
            <span class="icon"><i class="fa-solid fa-angle-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
          </a>
        </div>
        <div class="card-content">
          <div class="content">
            <p>Yes! The <a href="/business-subscription.html">Business subscription</a>
              ($200/month) allows you to run the complete ipapi.is API in your own infrastructure.
              The self-hosted server ships as a single native Linux binary with no runtime dependencies, requires
              only 4 GB of RAM, and handles more than 100,000 lookups per second on four-core hardware.</p>
            <p>Self-hosted lookups are unlimited, and the bundled update script downloads fresh databases daily and
              swaps them into the running server with zero downtime. Support is included.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-header">
          <p class="card-header-title">How accurate is the API?</p>
          <a class="card-header-icon">
            <span class="icon"><i class="fa-solid fa-angle-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
          </a>
        </div>
        <div class="card-content">
          <div class="content">
            <p>The accuracy of the API depends on the specific data point. While the general accuracy is <a
                href="/changelog.html">constantly improved</a>, some data is more accurate than others.</p>
            <ul>
              <li>WHOIS data: Very accurate, as it comes directly from the source (ARIN, APNIC, RIPE, AFRINIC,
                LACNIC).</li>
              <li>Geolocation: Very accurate at the country level and reasonably accurate at the city level.</li>
              <li>ASN data: Very accurate.</li>
              <li>Hosting/datacenter detection: Very accurate (superior to competitors).</li>
              <li>Tor detection: Very accurate.</li>
              <li>Proxy and VPN detection: Moderately accurate. Does not detect residential proxies or unknown VPN
                providers.</li>
            </ul>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-header">
          <p class="card-header-title">Why should we use ipapi.is and not competitors?</p>
          <a class="card-header-icon">
            <span class="icon"><i class="fa-solid fa-angle-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
          </a>
        </div>
        <div class="card-content">
          <div class="content">
            <p>You should test for yourself and verify with real benchmarks. See our
              <a href="/competitors.html">competitor comparison</a>,
              <a href="/blog/ip-geolocation-accuracy-benchmark.html">geolocation accuracy benchmark</a>, and
              <a href="/blog/ip-to-company-accuracy.html">IP-to-company accuracy study</a>. Key strengths of

              <li>VPN & Tor detection: Systematic exit-node enumeration updated daily.</li>

              <li>ASN metadata: Accurate <code>type</code> classification (hosting, isp, business, education, government, banking).</li>
              <li>Transparent pricing: Generous commercial free tier, non-expiring credits, and affordable unlimited self-hosting.</li>

      <div class="card">
        <div class="card-header">
          <p class="card-header-title">In the API, what is the difference between the company and
            asn objects?
          </p>
          <a class="card-header-icon">
            <span class="icon"><i class="fa-solid fa-angle-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
          </a>
        </div>
        <div class="card-content">
          <div class="content">
            <p>
              Simply put, the <code>company</code> object contains information about the organization that owns the IP
              address. The <code>asn</code> object, on the other hand, contains information about an autonomous
              system. An IP address can be part of an ASN through a route or prefix.
            </p>
            <p>
              If an IP address is part of an ASN, it does not necessarily mean that the IP address is owned by the
              organization associated with that ASN (although this is often the case). It only means that the ASN is
              responsible for routing the IP address and that the ASN has an assigned prefix or route that includes
              the IP address.
            </p>
            <p>
              The <code>company</code> object, on the other hand, contains ownership information about the IP address.
              This information is sourced from WHOIS records and describes the organization that owns the IP address
              in question.
            </p>

            <p>
              In summary:
            </p>

            <ul>
              <li>
                <code>company</code>: Contains ownership information about the queried IP address.
              </li>
              <li>
                <code>asn</code>: Contains information about the autonomous system that the queried IP address is
                part of. Usually the ASN organization is the same as the <code>company</code> organization, but this
                is not
                necessarily the case.
              </li>
            </ul>
